name: Vedanta Ltd.
business_summary: Post-demerger (2026) Vedanta Ltd is essentially a holding company for Hindustan Zinc (~61%) plus Zinc International (South Africa, Namibia, Ireland), the copper business, nickel, ferroalloys and incubator ventures; aluminium moved to Vedanta Aluminium Metal, and oil & gas, power and iron & steel to separately listed entities. Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue Rs26,356 cr, EBITDA Rs9,938 cr (+106%), of which Zinc India Rs9,243 cr (93%); profit from continuing operations Rs6,202 cr (+151%) but profit attributable to shareholders Rs3,650 cr (-33% q/q); net debt Rs3,675 cr (0.1x), cash Rs26,622 cr. First post-demerger dividend Rs5/share (Rs1,955 cr). Mcap Rs1.03 lakh cr.

revenue_mix.segment: Zinc India (Hindustan Zinc: zinc, lead, silver)
Copper, Zinc International, nickel, ferroalloys, other
revenue_mix.geography: India, Zambia, South Africa, Namibia, Ireland, UAE (India ~65% of group per screener About)

exposures.mechanism: Residual Vedanta Ltd keeps the copper business (smelting/refining plus Zambian mining via KCM, model knowledge) after the aluminium/oil & gas/power/steel demergers; copper segment size NOT disclosed in sources read (Q2 segment table not found). Assume copper ~8% of residual EBITDA ex-HZL (Rs800 cr/q annualised Rs3,200 cr vs total Rs39,700 cr): +10% copper on mining margin ~+25% of that = +Rs800 cr = +2% EBITDA, persistence 0.5, EV/MCap ~1.0 => +1.0; widened. Empirical +4.02 (t=2.1) but estimated over a period when VEDL included aluminium (pre-demerger), so stale.

evidence.note: Post-demerger Vedanta Ltd = HZL, Zinc International, copper, nickel, ferroalloys, incubator ventures

exposures.mechanism: EX-HZL channel only (HZL's zinc/silver exposure arrives through the holding_stake link HZL->VEDL, w 0.75, to avoid double count). Zinc International (Gamsberg, Black Mountain, Skorpion; ~0.3-0.4 Mt zinc, model knowledge) = ~12% of zinc volume of the group; +10% zinc ~ +Rs600 cr EBITDA on Rs39,700 cr annualised = +1.5% x0.6 persistence => +0.9.

evidence.note: Zinc India EBITDA Rs9,243 cr = 93% of consolidated EBITDA; Zinc International in residual

exposures.mechanism: STALE-DATA FLAG. Empirical +7.22 per SSU (t=3.2, strongest in pack) reflects 2021-26 when aluminium was ~half of VEDL EBITDA. Aluminium is now in Vedanta Aluminium Metal (VAML, listed June 2026) so fundamental exposure is ~0; residual +0.5 is sentiment/index co-movement (group stocks trade together; Vedanta Ltd shareholders hold VAML 1:1) and possible Cairn/other linkage. Assembler should NOT shrink toward +7.2.

evidence.note: VAML separate listed entity; 56.38% promoter stake

exposures.mechanism: Residual business is USD-priced (zinc, silver, copper); costs largely INR for HZL, USD/ZAR/NAD for Zinc International. HZL channel +2.2 per SSU (carried via link); ex-HZL, USD debt at parent (Vedanta Resources bonds are outside VEDL) and Zambian/SA costs. Net +2.0 on consolidated EBITDA +4% x persistence 0.5.

evidence.note: Net debt Rs3,675 cr, ND/EBITDA 0.1x; EBITDA Rs9,938 cr

exposures.mechanism: Group is a high-yield issuer: promoter shares (54.72% of VEDL, 56.38% of VAML) are encumbered with GLAS Agency for US$2.25bn/US$1bn financings and a US$400m bond tap (16 Sep 2026); parent Vedanta Resources depends on VEDL dividends (Rs5/share = Rs1,955 cr in Oct, 12.9% yield). +50 bp spreads raises parent refinancing cost (~US$5-6bn parent debt, model knowledge) => higher dividend demands and forced-sale risk. Weight is judgemental.

evidence.note: Promoter group encumbers 54.72% of Vedanta under US$2.25bn financing
First post-demerger interim dividend Rs5/share, Rs1,955 cr

exposures.mechanism: Dollar rates drive refinancing cost of Vedanta Resources notes and global metals risk appetite; 10y UST at 4.89% (+9% since 1 June). +25 bp => -0.8 on valuation and parent credit.
Dividend-yield stock (12.9% trailing); +25 bp on Indian cost of equity => ~-0.8. Direct interest bill small at VEDL (Rs696 cr/q; net debt 0.1x).

evidence.note: Dividend yield 12.9%, P/E 7.85, interest Rs696 cr in Q2

exposures.mechanism: Residual earnings are 93% Zinc India, so a royalty rise is ~0.6 x HZL's -1.5 plus copper/Zinc International royalties and Zambia royalty (a recurring tax risk). Look-through ~-1.2.

FIIs hold 15.8% and the stock is a high-volatility, high-beta name (price series not demerger-adjusted: 1y vol 111% and -48% 12m are artefacts of the aluminium/oil/power/steel demergers). +US$5bn quarterly net FPI inflow => relief rally in metals; record FPI outflow in CY2026 is a headwind.
Empirical -0.67 per +5 VIX points (t=-0.6, insignificant) and beta 1.1 to 1.3; consistent with a leveraged-at-parent, cyclical stock; weight set at empirical value.

company_links.mechanism: Vedanta holds ~60.7-61.8% of HZL (promoter holding 60.71% per screener, direct VEDL stake not separately verified). Look-through value 0.607 x Rs2,41,139 cr = ~Rs1.46 lakh cr, about 143% of VEDL's Rs1.03 lakh cr mcap (a deep holdco discount; VEDL also carries minorities' leakage, parent dividend/brand-fee outflow, and the rest of the business). A fixed-rupee discount would imply w=1.4, a proportional discount w=1.0; weekly regressions of VEDL on HZL give beta 0.54 (2021-26, pre-demerger mix), 0.66 (last 12m) and 0.77 since July 2026 (corr 0.84, 19 weeks). Central 0.75.

evidence.note: Zinc India = 93% of consolidated EBITDA, HZL ~60.71% owned
Vedanta divested 1.6% of HZL for ~Rs3,028 cr (headline)

company_links.mechanism: Same promoter (Vedanta Resources/Twin Star), identical shareholder base from the 1:1 demerger, shared encumbrance structure. Raw weekly regression of VEDL on VAML not available (20 weeks of VAML history); VAML on VEDL beta 0.46, corr 0.58. w = % move in VEDL per 1% move in VAML, shrunk for market component.

evidence.note: 56.38% promoter shares of Vedanta group entities encumbered

Q/Q and y/y comparisons are NOT like-for-like because of the demergers; screener TTM (sales Rs96,507 cr, NP Rs31,279 cr incl. other income Rs13,605 cr) mixes pre- and post-demerger periods and is unreliable.
